statement: Partition boundaries preserve exact declared-key semantics across median selection, persistence, restart/readback and routing: INTEGER keys beyond JavaScript Number safe range remain exact and correctly ordered; TEXT/BLOB boundaries retain their declared representation; persisted boundary rows carry enough type authority to decode without heuristic coercion; and legacy ambiguous boundaries are explicitly migrated or fail closed for revalidation before they can route.

constraints.statement: An INTEGER primary key above 2^53 survives split-median selection, persisted partition boundary representation, restart/readback and routing comparison without rounding, textual ambiguity or order inversion.
Boundary decoding uses declared/persisted key type authority; it does not infer INTEGER versus TEXT from lexical shape.

Do not globally enable SQLite safe-integer mode for all query results. Exact-integer handling is scoped to the boundary/median owner so unrelated JSON/result-size paths do not receive BigInt unexpectedly.
Existing ambiguous TEXT-era boundary rows are migrated with authoritative type information or fail closed until explicitly revalidated; old ambiguous rows never silently become routing authority.
Preserve the sealed A1 comparator contract, SQLite BINARY TEXT ordering, numeric/TEXT compatibility during migration, and actual KeyRange/PartitionResolver/QueryGroup/split-merge owner usage.
No Raft runtime, consensus, membership, formation or lifecycle behavior changes.
